attributes.body_ja:
「とは言（い）え」は、「確（たし）かに (A) だけど、だからといって (B) にはならない」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）です。この表現（ひょうげん）は (A) の内容（ないよう）を格助詞（かくじょし）「と」で引用（いんよう）し、それを副助詞（ふくじょし）「は」で話題（わだい）として取（と）り上（あ）げ、最後（さいご）に「言（い）え」（「言（い）う」の命令形（めいれいけい））を使（つか）って強（つよ）い主張（しゅちょう）を作（つく）っています。(A) の内容（ないよう）は話（はな）し手（て）がそうであると認（みと）めながらも、受（う）け入（い）れがたいと思（おも）っている事柄（ことがら）になります。

「とは言（い）え」は「と」で始（はじ）まるため、さまざまな言葉（ことば）に続（つづ）けて使（つか）うことができます。

通常（つうじょう）、(A) には一般的（いっぱんてき）に事実（じじつ）とされていることや、少（すく）なくとも話（はな）し手（て）が事実（じじつ）だと認識（にんしき）していることが入（はい）ります。
attributes.body:
とは言（い）え is one of the standard grammar patterns in Japanese that makes use of the imperative form in order to strongly state a point. It will often be translated as 'although (A), (B) will not change', or 'be that as it may, (B)'. Literally, it is just making use of the case-marking particle と in addition to the adverbial particle は to present (A) as a quote that the speaker acknowledges, but may not actually accept.

As this structure begins with と, it may be used at the end of any standard statement.

In most situations, the way that とはいえ will be used is like the English 'say that it is (A), that still doesn't change (B)'. (A) will generally be something that is true, or true as far as the speaker knows.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: These are both formal/written-style expressions that have the same fundamental meaning of 'even if one says'. In practice, both are used as a literary way to say 'although’, even if there is no explicit intention of quoting something that was said, e.g. ここは治安がいい（といえども・とはいえ）油断してはいけない ('Even though it's safe here, you mustn't be careless.').

second_relatable.title: とはいえ
second_relatable.meaning: Though, Although (I admit that), Be that as it may, Nonetheless

attributes.body: Both show concession, but differ in nuance. にせよ・にしろ makes a strong assertion that something holds regardless, as in 結果が悪いにしろ挑戦するべきだ (Even if the result is bad, you should try). とはいえ concedes a point but softens with that said, as in 難しいとはいえ不可能ではない (While it may be difficult, it’s not impossible).

attributes.body: にしろ～にしろ lists alternatives where the outcome stays the same, as in 成功するにしろ失敗するにしろ挑戦する価値がある (Whether you succeed or fail, it’s worth trying). とはいえ acknowledges something but introduces a contrasting fact, as in 難しいとはいえ不可能ではない (That said, it’s not impossible).

second_relatable.title: とはいえ
second_relatable.meaning: Though, Although (I admit that), Be that as it may, Nonetheless

attributes.body: とはいえ 'although (one could say)' specifically qualifies a statement by saying one thing might be true, but there is more to the matter, e.g. 日本人とはいえ、フランスで生まれ育った ('Though she may be Japanese, she was born and raised in France.'). であれ～であれ is specifically used when comparing multiple options, e.g. 日本人であれ外国人であれ、法律は守らないといけない ('No matter if you're Japanese or a foreigner, one must obey the law.').

first_relatable.meaning: Though, Although (I admit that), Be that as it may, Nonetheless

second_relatable.title: であれ〜であれ
second_relatable.meaning: Whether or, Or, No matter which, In either case

attributes.body: とはいえ and であれ are similar in that they both express a sort of contrast, but とはいえ 'although (one could say)' specifically qualifies a statement by saying one thing might be true, but there is more to the matter, e.g. 日本人とはいえ、フランスで生まれ育った ('Though she may be Japanese, she was born and raised in France.'). Though they can overlap in some cases, であれ 'even'/'no matter' is often used together with question words, e.g. 理由は何であれ 'no matter the reason', while とはいえ cannot be used this way.
